title: Impact on Singapore Due To Change in Government in Malaysia
what_it_is: Impact on Singapore Due To Change in Government in Malaysia

sections.label: New Malaysian Cabinet sworn in
sections.summary: Malaysia's new Cabinet led by Prime Minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob was sworn in on 21 August 2021, and Prime Minister Lee spoke with him the next morning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Its new Cabinet, led by Prime Minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob, was sworn in on 21 August 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lee spoke with Prime Minister Ismail Sabri the very next morning.

sections.label: Singapore-Malaysia COVID-19 cooperation
sections.summary: Singapore cooperated with Malaysia's previous government on COVID-19, setting up a Special Working Committee and launching travel arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: For example, we cooperated closely with the previous government led by former Prime Minister Muhyiddin Yassin to tackle the COVID-19 pandemic, including contributing medical supplies and test kits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We acted quickly in the early days of the pandemic to set up the Singapore-Malaysia Special Working Committee on COVID-19, which was co-chaired by Senior Minister and the Coordinating Minister for National Security Teo Chee Hean and then-Senior Minister and Minister of Defence of Malaysia Ismail Sabri, in order to coordinate both countries’ measures to respond to COVID-19, and minimise disruptions to our companies, workers and citizens.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We also launched several travel arrangements, such as the safe movement of cargo trucks, the Periodic Commuting Arrangement for workers and a framework for Death and Critically Ill Emergency Visits.

sections.label: Singapore-Malaysia bilateral projects commitment
sections.summary: Singapore remains committed to ties with Malaysia and to bilateral projects including the RTS Link, which resumes service at end-2026.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Singapore remains committed to maintaining a constructive and positive relationship with the current Malaysian government.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We will also follow through with our commitments on bilateral projects and our partnerships on the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link Project and COVID-19 border control measures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: On the RTS Link Project, Singapore and Malaysia reached an agreement to resume the project in July last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The RTS Link will be a game changer when it commences service at the end of 2026.

sections.label: Recognising each other's vaccine certificates
sections.summary: Both sides are currently working towards recognising each other's vaccine certificates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: For example, both sides are currently working towards recognising each other’s vaccine certificates.
